note: Words: Bate & Dudfield (2019) PeerJ 7:e6330, Table 1 ('PCA loadings for each item on the SRQ'), 20 statements transcribed verbatim from the Europe PMC full-text XML (PMC6360075), including the source's singular 'television program.' and its typographic apostrophes. Codes: data/bate_2019_srq.py keeps the deposit's own column names SRQ01..SRQ20 (peerj-07-6330-s001.xlsx, sheets EXP1/EXP2); the .xlsx has no label level and no codebook, so code->text is assigned by Table 1 row order (paper_order) -- the paper never states Table 1 is in questionnaire order. Anchors: the paper says only that '1 represented strongly disagree and 5 represented strongly agree' for half the items and 'the remaining items were reverse-coded'; no intermediate labels and no instructions are printed, so resp 2-4 option_text and instructions are blank. The stored items are ALREADY reverse-scored: summed items reproduce Table 2's SRQ mean (SD) exactly (Exp1 89.64 (8.11), Exp2 78.91 (9.94)) and equal the deposit's 'SRQ ALL' column row for row, and all inter-item correlations are >= -0.07. So for the ten negatively worded statements (SRQ01,03,04,05,08,10,11,12,17,19) resp 1='strongly agree' and 5='strongly disagree'; for the other ten the reverse. That per-item direction is an inference from the scoring, not a label in the source. Rights: the SRQ was developed in this paper (CC BY 4.0, PeerJ); no rights statement restricting it located. instrument_rights_register.csv's '^srq' code patterns hit the WHO SRQ-20 and CSDT SRQ rows -- both are different instruments sharing the acronym; neither applies. Mapping check (Step 5b, PARTIAL): see verification_bate_2019_srq.csv. Note the published Table 1 loading VALUES do not reproduce cell-for-cell from the deposit under any common rotation (e.g. items 1, 5, 11 print no loading at all but load .62/.66/.52 here), though the variance explained (27.35/8.23/6.81%) and the high-loader pattern do.
public_note: Codes SRQ01-SRQ20 are matched to the paper's Table 1 statements by row order, which the data support at the cluster level but cannot confirm item by item; all 20 items are stored reverse-scored where needed so that higher always means better self-reported face recognition (for the ten negatively worded items resp 1 = strongly agree).
